## Motion Blur

#### Motion Blur { #unreal-motionblur }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:motionBlur</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealmotionBlur_41a</code></dd></div></dl>

Average sub-frames over the camera shutter (shutter:open/close) when something moves. Depth of field comes from the camera's fStop and focusDistance.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="motion-blur"></div>

#### Motion Samples { #unreal-motionsamples }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>16</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>1 to 64</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:motionSamples</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealmotionSamples_06a</code></dd></div></dl>

Sub-frames per frame. Path Tracer samples and realtime warmup frames are divided between them; too few show discrete copies of fast objects.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="motion-blur-samples"></div>

#### Amount { #unreal-postprocess-motionbluramount }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.5</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurAmount</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessMotionBlurAmount_tubl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Strength of motion blur, 0:off

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-motion-blur-amount"></div>

#### Max { #unreal-postprocess-motionblurmax }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>5</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurMax</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessMotionBlurMax_xpbl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

max distortion caused by motion blur, in percent of the screen width, 0:off

#### Target FPS { #unreal-postprocess-motionblurtargetfps }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>30</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 120</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurTargetFPS</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessMotionBlurTargetFPS_pzbl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Defines the target FPS for motion blur. Makes motion blur independent of actual frame rate and relative to the specified target FPS instead. Higher target FPS results in shorter frames, which means shorter shutter times and less motion blur. Lower FPS means more motion blur. A value of zero makes the motion blur dependent on the actual frame rate.

#### Per Object Size { #unreal-postprocess-motionblurperobjectsize }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:MotionBlurPerObjectSize</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessMotionBlurPerObjectSize_75bl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

The minimum projected screen radius for a primitive to be drawn in the velocity pass, percentage of screen width. smaller numbers cause more draw calls, default: 4%

## MegaLights

#### MegaLights { #unreal-postprocess-bmegalights }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:bMegaLights</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessbMegaLights_ombl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Allows forcing MegaLights on or off for this volume, regardless of the project setting for MegaLights. MegaLights will stochastically sample lights, which allows many shadow casting lights to be rendered efficiently, with a consistent and low GPU cost. When MegaLights is enabled, other direct lighting algorithms like Deferred Shading will no longer be used, and other shadowing methods like Ray Traced Shadows, Distance Field Shadows and Shadow Maps will no longer be used. MegaLights requires Hardware Ray Tracing and Shader Model 6.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-megalights"></div>

#### MegaLights - High Quality Translucency { #unreal-postprocess-megalightsfrontlayertranslucency }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:MegaLightsFrontLayerTranslucency</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessMegaLightsFrontLayerTranslucency_vlcl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Whether to use high quality direct lighting on the front layer of translucent surfaces. Other layers will use the lower quality Translucency Lighting Volume. Increases GPU cost when enabled.

#### Samples per Pixel { #unreal-cvar-r-megalights-numsamplesperpixel }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>4</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cvar:r:MegaLights:NumSamplesPerPixel</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcvarrMegaLightsNumSamplesPerPixel_l4bebk</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Number of samples per downsampled pixel for the opaque lighting pass. Final number of samples depends also on the downsampling mode. Supported values: 1, 2 and 4. Console variable r.MegaLights.NumSamplesPerPixel (process-wide).

| Value | Label |
|---|---|
| `1` | 1 |
| `2` | 2 |
| `4` | 4 |

#### Default Shadow Method { #unreal-cvar-r-megalights-defaultshadowmethod }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Ray Tracing</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cvar:r:MegaLights:DefaultShadowMethod</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcvarrMegaLightsDefaultShadowMethod_75bebk</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

The default shadowing method for MegaLights, unless over-ridden on the light component. 0 - Ray Tracing. Preferred method, which guarantees fixed MegaLights cost and correct area shadows, but is dependent on the BVH representation quality. 1 - Virtual Shadow Maps. Has a significant per light cost, but can cast shadows directly from the Nanite geometry using rasterization. Console variable r.MegaLights.DefaultShadowMethod (process-wide).

| Value | Label |
|---|---|
| `0` | Ray Tracing |
| `1` | Virtual Shadow Maps |
